newsitem.title: UKRAINE: After Kohl, Ukraine gets backing from Clinton.
newsitem.headline: After Kohl, Ukraine gets backing from Clinton.

text.p: Ukraine has won support for its economic reform programme from U.S. President Bill Clinton, President Leonid Kuchma's office said on Thursday.
A statement from Kuchma's office said Clinton had promised in a letter to fulfil promises of international aid for Ukrainian reform.

"The United States has worked intensively with the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank and G7 nations for allocation $1.9 billion in aid to Ukraine in 1996," the statement quoted Clinton's letter as saying. "The American side will further allocate its bilateral assistance to Ukraine."
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl had backed Ukraine's reform efforts during a two-day visit to Ukraine this week.
"We want to be partners in Europe," he said on Tuesday. "Ukraine can be a bridge to the countries in the east and the south of our continent."
Washington has given Kiev $330 million in aid this year and $675 million in credits. Ukraine is world's third largest recepient of U.S. aid after Israel and Egypt.
